reason: Start with the filtering goal: the picture shows blood approaching the filter, so this should reveal what passes through.
expectation: I expect small substances, including useful glucose and waste, to pass through while large blood cells and proteins stay in the blood.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would begin the route to the bladder, but I want to see filtering first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose through along with waste, so the recovery tube is the next useful step.
reaction: It was interesting that filtering doesn't just remove waste.
reason: The recovery tube's picture shows useful substances moving back toward the blood.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much water to return to the blood, with waste remaining in the fluid.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the drainage route, but I want to follow the filtered fluid first.

effect: Useful substances and much water return to blood, leaving a smaller amount of waste-containing fluid to collect.
reaction: The recovery step made the filter's purpose clearer.
reason: The ureters lead from the kidneys toward the bladder, so they start the collection route.
expectation: I expect the ureters to attach to the kidneys, leaving a connection for the bladder.

alternatives.reason: The bladder is also needed, but the ureters appear to connect it to the kidneys.

effect: The ureters now connect to the kidney outlets and extend downward, ready for the bladder.
reaction: That matched the route I expected.
reason: The bladder is the only offered combination and completes the route the ureters point toward.
expectation: I expect the bladder to attach to the ureters so fluid can travel from the kidneys into it.

effect: The kidneys now have a continuous route through the ureters to the bladder; the organs still need connecting to the body.
reaction: Seeing the bladder stretch as it fills made its storage role clearer.
reason: I want to follow the remaining kidney fluid into the completed collection route.
expectation: I expect the waste-containing fluid to travel through the ureters and collect as urine in the bladder.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the urinary organs to the body is also a goal, but I want to follow the fluid first.

effect: The remaining urine reaches the bladder while blood continues through a separate vessel. The urinary organs still need to connect to the body.
reaction: The separate routes make the result easy to follow.
reason: Connecting the kidneys and bladder to the body is the remaining goal and the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the urinary organs to be placed in the body and connected to its blood supply.

effect: The urinary organs are connected to the body's circulation, completing the chapter.
reaction: The finished picture brings the blood and urine routes together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following filtered fluid into the recovery tube was most worthwhile: it showed why useful water and substances have to return to the blood.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bladder was straightforward and the only offered combination, so it felt more like assembly than a decision.

surprise.text: The filter let useful glucose through along with waste, rather than simply picking out waste.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals explained the connections, although the bladder fitting was predictable.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter: following the fluid through filtering, recovery and collection made the system easier to understand, though some assembly steps were predictable.
